text: Course registration shouldn't be a race against the refresh button.
This is Pusula, a redesign of our university's student information system.
Everything starts with today: your classes, a live line for right now, and the next deadline counting down.
If your registration still has a problem, you see it before it's too late.
The old system hides forty-eight untitled menu items.
Here there are a few clear sections, and everything else is one search away.
On the registration page, every rule is checked while you choose, not after.
Deniz adds the course he failed last year.
Two electives clash. Instead of trying sections one by one, he asks for a conflict-free set.
One click, and the timetable is fixed.
With every check passed, he sends it to his advisor.
Ece is a first-year student who hasn't registered yet. She adds her curriculum with one click.
Then she simply writes the week she wants: Friday off, and nothing before ten.
Pusula tries every combination of sections and ranks the best timetables.
The top one even frees up Wednesday. One click applies it.
The biggest change is pre-selection. Next semester, you won't need to be online when registration opens.
You rank your courses, pick preferred sections, and add backups in case a course is full or doesn't open.
Pusula checks the plan in advance, so there are no surprises later.
For the demo, we simulate registration opening in ten seconds. On a phone, you could close the app now.
Registration opens, and a notification arrives.
Every decision is explained: which section was full, which course didn't open, and which backup took its place.
Graduation progress finally works, with a map of every course you still need.
And Pusula installs like an app on your phone, in light or dark mode.
Pusula. Plan once, and register without the race.
